subject: Chemistry
title: Leaded Gasoline: A Global Poisoning
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Leaded Gasoline: A Global Poisoning.

hook.text: For 70 years, lead was added to gasoline. It poisoned billions of people worldwide—and the man who invented it knew.

buildup.text: Thomas Midgley Jr. discovered that tetraethyl lead stopped engine knocking. GM and Standard Oil began selling leaded gas in 1923.

discovery.text: Lead from exhaust settled into soil, water, and lungs. Blood lead levels in Americans peaked at 6x safe limits in the 1970s.

twist.text: Midgley also invented CFCs. One man created two of the 20th century's worst environmental disasters.

climax.text: Leaded gasoline was banned globally by 2021. Blood lead levels dropped 75% within years of each country's ban.

punchline.text: Lead in every tank for 70 years. The world's IQ may have dropped because of one additive.

quiz.question: What is notable about Thomas Midgley Jr.'s inventions?
options: He invented both leaded gasoline and CFCs—two major environmental disasters
He won the Nobel Prize for both inventions
He was the first to warn about lead's toxicity

details.summary: Tetraethyl lead was added to gasoline from the 1920s to boost engine performance despite early evidence of severe lead toxicity. For over seventy years, automobile exhaust dispersed lead globally, lowering IQ scores, increasing crime rates, and contaminating soil and water worldwide.
details.whyItMatters: Leaded gasoline is considered one of the largest mass poisoning events in human history. Its phase-out, completed globally in 2021, demonstrated how economic interests can delay action on known chemical hazards.
takeaways: Tetraethyl lead was known to be toxic before it was commercialized
Lead exposure reduced average IQ scores globally by several points
The global phase-out was completed in 2021, nearly a century later

faq.question: Why was lead added to gasoline if it was known to be toxic?
faq.answer: Lead eliminated engine knocking cheaply and effectively. General Motors and Standard Oil, which held the patent, promoted it aggressively while suppressing health concerns..

faq.question: Is there evidence that leaded gasoline actually increased crime rates?
faq.answer: Multiple studies across countries found strong correlations between childhood lead exposure and violent crime rates twenty years later. Lead damages the prefrontal cortex, which governs impulse control. The crime decline of the 1990s temporally matches the lead phase-out of the 1970s.
